### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/connector-slack`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **193** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**117** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2`.

⛔ **22** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`, `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 55 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **28** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4119acc30162dc12dcc876fdface88a8d182b62f` — the merge of head `938fa8f8c8509655ef8fc84855b2866b1821850b` into base `2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4119acc30162dc12dcc876fdface88a8d182b62f && git checkout 4119acc30162dc12dcc876fdface88a8d182b62f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2 938fa8f8c8509655ef8fc84855b2866b1821850b && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2 && git merge --no-ff 938fa8f8c8509655ef8fc84855b2866b1821850b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

  - One sentence is imprecise (note 1).
- **Tests assert ADR-0112 `code` and `status`.** Each refusal pins `[code, status]`: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR, 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND and 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT. The 409 also checks `userMessage` in `en` and `fr`. Every call runs `envelopeViolations(body)` → `[]`.
- **Tests I ran on 73b116f0** (after `pnpm turbo run build` of the deps, exit 0):
  - service-messaging: `slack-links.integration.test.ts` 13/13, `slack-channel.test.ts` 10/10, `recipient-reach.test.ts` 3/3, `messaging-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` 3/3.
  - plugin-approvals: `approval-requested-slack-dm.integration.test.ts` 6/6.
  - spec: `platform-object-names.test.ts` 14/14.

  - The `setup.write` check disabled (`if (false && admin …)`): "(5) every administrator door demands setup.write…" went red, 1 failed / 12 passed.
  - The Slack `reachableRecipients` made to return every recipient: `slack-channel.test.ts` went red, 1 failed / 9 passed. In plugin-approvals, the "proposed link" and "none link" cases went red, 2 failed / 4 passed.
- **Dogfood and MCP.** No MCP tool description moved. No send or write moved after a response. Grepping `packages/qa/dogfood/test` finds no case that reads `suppressed_channels`, delivery channels of `approval.requested`, or Slack.
- **Follow-ups exist and are open.** #35791: make connector-slack's static token optional. #35809: proposal cooldown, cache and 429. #35810: a stale proposal still blocks the next holder of that email.

**Non-blocking notes:**
1. **Changeset sentence (owed before landing, text only).** "`approval.requested` now asks for `slack` beside inbox and e-mail" leaves out its condition. The code asks only while the `slack` channel is mounted (plugin-approvals: `getChannel?.('slack') ? ['slack'] : []`), that is, while ConnectorSlackPlugin is composed. Add "when the `slack` channel is registered" or the like. This is not a CHANGES round on its own: fold it into the seat's contract-read round, and L1 delta-reads that line only.

The `resolveChannelAvailability` docblock (messaging-service.ts:~1594, ~653) still says availability is "answered from in-memory composition state". That is no longer true for every channel, so the comment is now stale.
4. **Trigger removals without an actor.** A trigger removal with no session user (`removeAllOf(…, actor undefined)`) is audited as the system. That is consistent with the audit writer's "absence stays absence" rule. The changeset's "every write names who acted" holds for human-initiated writes.

### Findings

**F1 (must-fix): `Metadata-protocol: none` is wrong, and with it the level.**
- `messaging-service-plugin.ts:641` registers the `slack` channel provider at `kernel:ready` on every composition. Only the mount waits for connector-slack. So `getKnownChannels()` (`messaging-service.ts:722`) lists `slack` everywhere.

**S1 (should-fix): two existing doors answer differently on every deployment, and the body says they do not.**

Both now list `slack`: `configured: false` without connector-slack, `configured: true` wherever it is composed, including an organization with no install.

**Nits**

The permission and the token are the two things the addendum says step 2 names. The cite fix matches N4 of `7024764224`. The status line, points 1 to 3 and the riders are untouched. No ruled text moved.

### ② Semver level

Wrong at this head: F1. All five published packages the diff touches are in the changeset, and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stands. The two spec registry rows alone are `none` and `patch` (precedent: `sys_unit`, #35581); the protocol kind comes from the `notify` channel, not from the registry.
